major_findings: Ridership dev subsample: 1,207,832 total rides across 200,000 records, 140 routes and 59 dates (2023-01-01 to 2023-02-28).
Ridership is concentrated: the top 10 routes account for 24.6781% of total ridership (coefficient of variation 1.039158).
Mean daily ridership is higher on weekdays (23,717.047619) than weekends (12,453.882353).
CJTP (customer-weighted) averages 69.583452% across 67,943 records spanning 2017-08-01 to 2026-06-01.
Peak CJTP (69.394873%) is lower than Off-Peak (69.716629%), i.e. journeys run less on-time at peak.
CJTP falls as additional travel time rises (Pearson r = -0.776963, n = 67942; association, not causation).
Stop network: 6,281 unique physical stops across 8,664 route-stop associations.
13 project route(s) have no stop associations in the cleaned data (left absent, not fabricated).
Route geometry: 206,338 features covering 142/142 project routes (100.0%).
Across project routes, ridership vs stop count shows Pearson r = 0.584246 (n = 128); association only.
119/142 project routes (83.802817%) appear in all three of ridership, stops and CJTP.

limitations: The processed ridership extract (mta_ridership_dev.parquet) is a development subsample: 200,000 records spanning only 2023-01-01 to 2023-02-28 (59 distinct service dates) with timestamps bucketed to 12 even hours (0,2,...,22). It does NOT support meaningful 24-hour / diurnal ridership pattern claims; hourly totals are reported descriptively only, and no continuous hourly-profile figure is drawn.
No 24-hour / diurnal ridership pattern is claimed; hourly totals are descriptive only (12 even-hour buckets).
Ridership covers 140/142 project routes; absent routes (J90, J99) carry no fabricated rows.
CJTP covers 120/142 project routes and has 1 missing CJTP value(s), excluded (not imputed).
Route geometry is analyzed from processing_report.json metadata only; the 2.3 GB GeoJSON is not parsed, so per-feature geometry characteristics (length, vertices, bbox) are not computed.
CJTP spans monthly aggregates 2017-2026 while ridership is a Jan-Feb 2023 subsample; the route-level ridership-vs-CJTP association therefore compares different time windows.
All correlations are measures of association and do not imply causation.
scipy is not installed, so correlation p-values are omitted; each correlation reports its sample size n so significance can still be judged.
